issues.body:
Within the same example the other placeholders are self-describing angle-bracket forms (`<uuid>`, `<owner/repo@run>`), while `account` is now an opaque literal `0123456789abcdef`. A reader skimming only this fence cannot tell that the value is `sha256(handle + ':' + PROVENANCE_SALT)[:16]` rather than a literal constant or a real account identifier; the explanation lives far away in the Security posture section (locked decision 22a).

This is deliberately filed as a nit, not a defect: an angle-bracket placeholder would NOT be a valid substitute here, because `select-and-claim.ACCOUNT_FINGERPRINT_RE` / `lease_schema.ACCOUNT` fullmatch `[0-9a-f]{16}` and a `<fingerprint>` token would not match. Showing a concrete hex literal is the right way to convey the enforced shape, and JSON has no comment syntax to annotate it inline. The change is correct and complete as written; nothing here blocks the merge.
issues.fix_hint: Optional only. Add one sentence of prose immediately below the fenced block, e.g.: "`account` is the salted fingerprint `sha256(handle + ':' + PROVENANCE_SALT)[:16]` -- 16 hex characters, never a raw `[redacted-account]` handle (locked decision 22a); `validate_lease_account_identities` drops any row that does not fullmatch that shape." Leave the literal inside the JSON fence unchanged so it continues to depict the enforced shape.
issues.title: Fingerprint placeholder is not self-describing next to the angle-bracket placeholders around it

verdict.summary:
Docs-only, one-line fix to the lease-ledger JSON example in README.md, changing the illustrative `account` value from the raw handle `[redacted-account]` to the 16-hex-character placeholder `0123456789abcdef`. Verified against the code rather than the prose: `scripts/select-and-claim.py:391` defines `ACCOUNT_FINGERPRINT_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{16}")` and `account_fingerprint()` (line 394) returns `sha256(f"{handle}:{salt}")[:16]`, failing closed when `PROVENANCE_SALT` or the handle is missing; `scripts/lease_schema.py:17` carries the identical `ACCOUNT` regex. The ledger therefore stores a SALTED FINGERPRINT, never a handle -- `validate_lease_account_identities()` (line 402) actively DROPS any row whose `account` is not a 16-hex fullmatch, which is exactly what the old `[redacted-account]` example depicted. So the pre-change README contradicted an enforced invariant and would have led an agent following it verbatim to write a row that the next CAS write silently discards. README's own Security posture section (locked decision 22a, ~line 880) already states that each ledger record names an account by `sha256(handle + ':' + PROVENANCE_SALT)[:16]` ONLY; this diff makes the example consistent with it. The new value is exactly 16 lowercase hex characters, so it fullmatches both regexes.

No trust check is weakened: nothing in `scripts/`, `.github/workflows/`, `policy/` or `orchestration/` is touched, no self-test is deleted or relaxed, and no default-allow path is opened. No test-validity concern arises (no test changed); `scripts/readme-runbook-check.py` correlates only `toml` runbook fences and `--account-handle [redacted-account]` patterns within an enrolment section, so this `json` fence in the Lease-based claim section is outside its scope and the suite is unaffected. Security: the placeholder is a synthetic, obviously-sequential digest-shaped string, not a credential and not a real fingerprint -- it is unreversible to a handle without the salt, so nothing token-shaped or PII… [truncated 266 chars]
